adds.title: LGBT rights in Turkey - Wikipedia
adds.summary: Wikipedia's 'LGBT rights in Turkey' page, the national framework that governs Sakarya (a Marmara-region province where national law applies): homosexuality has been decriminalised in Turkey since 1858, and sex-reassignment surgery has been legal since 1988, but legal gender recognition still requires a court's permission under Civil Code Article 40 with the applicant at least 18, unmarried and holding a medical report from a state-designated hospital. The Turkish military bars homosexuals from service and treats homosexuality as a 'psychosexual' illness, and Istanbul Pride drew roughly 100,000 participants in 2013-2014 before the 2015-2018 parades were banned by local authorities. No province-specific rule for Sakarya is recorded here; the provisions above apply nationwide, including to Sakarya's residents and visitors.

adds.title: Factsheet on leaked law proposals against LGBTI+ rights in Türkiye - Amnesty International
adds.summary: Amnesty International's November 2025 factsheet analyses the leaked '11th Judicial Package', a 66-page draft amending the Turkish Penal Code, Civil Code and six other laws that was leaked to Turkish media in mid-October 2025. It is the third set of proposed legal amendments targeting LGBTI+ rights in 2025, the earlier two having stalled in Parliament. The draft would raise the minimum age for legal gender recognition procedures from 18 to 25 and add further conditions; Amnesty warns it would criminalise LGBTI+ people and those advocating for their rights, and would severely restrict or make impossible trans and gender-diverse people's access to gender-affirming healthcare. These are nationwide proposals that would apply within every province including Sakarya, whose record already notes the leaked October 2025 package.
